CFDocument.title: GACE® Special Education Adapted Curriculum Assessment Test

CFItems.fullStatement: Development and Characteristics of Learners
Assessment
Foundations and Professional Responsibilities
Planning the Learning Environment and Social Interactions
Instruction
*Objective 1: Understands and applies knowledge of human development and behavior*
*Objective 1: Understands and applies knowledge of curriculum development and planning*
*Objective 2: Understands and applies knowledge of managing the learning environment*
*Objective 1: Understands and applies knowledge of effective and appropriate teaching strategies and techniques*
*Objective 1: Understands terminology and applies knowledge of the uses of various assessments and their results*
*Objective 1: Understands and applies knowledge of educational rights for students with learning disabilities*
*Objective 2: Understands and applies knowledge of professional foundations of special education*
Understands human development and behavior; e.g., cognitive, language, social/emotional, psychological, academic, and physical development
Understands and differentiates among theoretical approaches to student learning and motivation

Identifies the basic characteristics and defining factors for each of the major disability categories under which 3 through 21-year-olds may be eligible for services under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA)
Understands the impact of disabilities on individuals, families, and society across the life span
Understands how language, cultural, and gender differences affect the identification process
Understands co-occurring conditions
Recognizes how family systems and the role of families contribute to the development of an individual with a disability; e.g., academic performance, social skills, interests, values
Demonstrates the influences that may affect the development and achievement of an individual with a disability; e.g., environmental factors, societal influences
Understands the characteristics of lesson plans

Knows the elements of lesson plans; e.g., objectives and goals; prerequisite knowledge; materials, technology, and procedures; motivation and student engagement; guided and independent practice; summarization, assessment, and reflection
Develops learning objectives that are measurable/observable and appropriate
Knows the means of providing access to the curriculum
Knows how to organize the learning environment
Understands how to manage student behavior
Understands theory and practice of effective classroom management
Knows how to design and maintain a safe and supportive classroom environment that promotes student achievement
Knows, understands, and applies instructional strategies and techniques
Recognizes grouping formats that ensure individual academic success
Implements strategies to facilitate the maintenance and generalization of concepts learned, considering students’ ages and abilities
Selects and implements research-based interventions for individual students
Understands the selection and implementation of supplementary curriculums
Demonstrates knowledge and implementation of functional curriculums
Identifies options for assistive technology
Demonstrates knowledge of transitions and transition planning
Recognizes evidence-based assessments that are effective and appropriate
Knows the definitions and uses of various assessments
Interprets assessment results
Understands and uses the results of assessments
Knows federal definitions
Knows federal requirements for the referral and identification process
Knows federal safeguards of the rights of stakeholders (parents, local education agency [LEA], students, teachers, related service providers)
Knows the components of a legally defensible Individualized Education Program (IEP)
Knows major legislation that affects the field of special education; e.g., Public Law 94-142, IDEA 2004, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, Americans with Disabilities Act
Understands the roles and responsibilities of the special education teacher
Understands the roles and responsibilities of other professionals who deliver related services (e.g., physical therapist, occupational therapist, speech-language pathologist)
Understands strengths and limitations of various collaborative approaches within the general classroom and the special education classroom
Communicates to stakeholders the progress of students, using language and terms the stakeholders will likely understand
Identifies potential bias issues that may affect teaching and interactions with students and their families; e.g., personal, familial, cultural, systemic
